html:
SMTO-TSK-0011 — These settings were changed somewhere else

GUID: 69c6d017-197c-4db2-813c-38a27d95eb3e
Slug: run-settings-changed
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • Someone or something changed these settings after you opened them, perhaps in another tab. To avoid overwriting that newer change, SMTO didn't save yours.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page, or close and reopen the settings panel you were using. This loads the newest saved version, including the change made elsewhere.
  2. Look at the current values before changing anything. If another browser tab has the same settings open, close it. The newer change may already be what you wanted, and a second open tab can keep making your view out of date.
  3. If your change is still needed, make it again in the reloaded panel. Now your edit is based on the latest version, so SMTO can save it safely.

What success looks like

  • The setting saves and stays at the value you chose after you reload the page.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If it keeps happening, someone or some script may be changing the same settings at the same time; find out who before editing again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The settings edit carried an expected policy revision that no longer matches the saved one (for example another tab or update changed the run's settings, Agent Checks or capabilities first), so it was rejected as stale.

What this means

  • The supplied expected policy revision differs from authoritative state, or effective capability/selection authority changed after its grant snapshot. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The supplied expected policy revision differs from authoritative state, or effective capability/selection authority changed after its grant snapshot.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare expected and current revision plus effective authority; do not overwrite intervening changes blindly.

How to fix it

  • The submitted policy_revision differs from the run's current revision (or the capability/guard state changed after the editor loaded). Re-read the current policy for the run or scope, compare it with the intended edit, and submit again with the new revision; never resend the old revision.
  • Refresh the current settings and review the intended edit against the new revision before applying it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A freshly reviewed edit validates against the current intended policy state.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
